title: Allowable Floor Area Increases

baseline.text: Under the IBC, what is the simplified form of the frontage increase formula (If) when the open space width equals or exceeds 30 feet?

options.text: If = F/P × 30, which applies when the open space is consistently maintained
If = 0.25 − F/P, applicable only under specific zoning conditions
If = F/P, used when no additional modifications are required

baseline.rationale: Option A (F/P × 30) drops both the threshold subtraction and the division by 30. Option C (0.25 − F/P) reverses the subtraction. Option D (F/P) omits the threshold subtraction entirely. All three are common errors that produce wrong answers in frontage calculations.

proposed.rationale: Option A (F/P × 30) drops both the threshold subtraction and the division by 30. Option C (0.25 − F/P) reverses the subtraction. Option D (F/P) omits the threshold subtraction entirely. All three are common errors that produce wrong answers in frontage calculations.
proposed.explanation: When the open-space width reaches the 30-foot cap, the frontage formula no longer rewards additional width. The simplified result keeps the frontage-to-perimeter ratio and subtracts the 0.25 threshold, so “If = F/P − 0.25” is the defensible answer. The other choices either multiply by the cap, reverse the subtraction, or omit the threshold.

evidence: Explanation derived from existing rationale and preserved correct option; no answer-key or option changes.
